Q: Assign Normal Distribution Function to an Array A:

Firstly, Type Mismatch error means that the (Worksheet) function does not return a Variant which is needed due to the custom function definition. The worksheet function returns a Double.

And secondly, "Object Required" appears because only an object should be Set. And the worksheet function does not return an object. As stated above, it returns a double.

My following answer is based on the assumption that the variables name you used really mean something (Range Average, Range Standard Deviation). In such a case, VBA is able to return an array if you transform the range in an array (inside the function). I mean an array calculated for each range cell, using global range Average and Standard Deviation.

In such circumstances, your function needs to be looking as:


Function NormDistr(r As Range, average As Double, std As Double) As Variant

 NormDistr = Application.Norm_Dist(r.value, average, std, False)
             'it works only replacing WorksheetFunctionn with Application...

End Function

And it can be called in the next way (I used a specific range, you need to use yours):

Sub NormDistrArray()
  Dim arrND, r As Range
  Set r = Range("H2:H13") 'use here your necessary range
  arrND = NormDistr(r, WorksheetFunction.average(r), WorksheetFunction.StDev(r))

  Debug.Print UBound(arrND) 'it returns the array number of elements
  Debug.Print Join(Application.Transpose(arrND), vbCrLf) 'it returns the array elements separated by VbCrLf
  r.Offset(, 1).value = arrND 'it returns one column to the right of the initial range
End Sub

In order to see the return in Immediate Window, you need to press `Ctrl + G`, being in VBE (Visual Basic Editor)

Or even a nicer solution, placing only the range argument to the function:

Sub TestNormDistrBis()
 Dim r As Range, arrND As Variant
 
 Set r = Range("$H$2:$H$13")
 arrND = NormDistrBis(r) 'place the function result in an array
 r.Offset(, 2).value = arrND 'drop the array content two columns to the right of the initial range
End Sub

Function NormDistrBis(r As Range) As Variant 
 NormDistrBis = Application.Norm_Dist(r.value, WorksheetFunction.average(r), WorksheetFunction.StDev(r), False)
End Function

Q: how to find primary key for table in mysql A:

The query below gets the part_no and its number of appearances; if you see two or more, part_no can't be your primary key, and you have to select another. Make sure part_no IS NOT NULL as you can't have null primary keys.

select part_no, count(*) as appearances
from inventory
group by part_no

If you want to know it faster because of many rows:

select max(appearances)
from ( select part_no, count(*) as appearances
       from inventory
       group by part_no )

If max is 1 you are OK. If not, add another column to the group by and select and do the same. Then you can determine the column(s) in your primary key. You can change it with alter table or a GUI.

Q: Android Studio gradle dependencies A:

For small projects and quick tests you can hardcode the versions like group:name:version. However for larger projects specially those with multiple modules, the seocnd way (libs.xxx) is the much cleaner and more reliable and scalable.

Actully in second way, the versions are maneged centrally in gradle/libs.versions.toml. This is how this file centralizes the versions:

[versions]
appcompat = "1.7.1"

[libraries]
appcompat = { group = "androidx.appcompat", name = "appcompat", version.ref = "appcompat" }

...

Then use it in build.gradle:

implementation libs.appcompat

Q: CreateFile with FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING but not FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH A:

This flags controlling different operations and layers in OS.

FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH - affects only write operations. Each buffer you pass in WriteFile* fuctions will be immediately flushed on disk. It's action different when file is local (working ok) or when file is on smb share (working ugly on large, don't use it).

FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING - indicates that programmer is responsible to to read/write file in large chunks (more 64kbytes, or even N megabytes) and internal OS buffers must be disabled (because it is useless on large read/write ops)
